title: Shared native worktree cache
objective: Make fresh parallel worktrees reuse content-addressed immutable native dependency and addon builds safely, so required validation does not rebuild GMP, FLINT, OpenBLAS, and graph or fail because an addon is absent.

handoff.summary: Added a verified content-addressed cache for FLINT and graph dependency prefixes and ABI-specific addons, shared through the Git common directory and restored automatically by parallel:new. Native validation now provisions through the cache and builds the root distribution before testing; changed-file checks use the same path. Cache publication, corruption handling, stale-lock recovery, local-copy isolation, key invalidation, and real process concurrency have focused coverage. A real Linux x64 cold build took 6m45s, while a complete warm restore took 1.5s; the retained cache is 212 MiB.
risks: Windows x64, Linux arm64, and macOS arm64 behavior is designed into keying, path handling, pnpm invocation, and atomic replacement, but the corresponding CI runners remain the final platform oracle.
The cache has no pruning policy yet, so distinct valid toolchain and source identities accumulate until removed manually.
Filesystems without copy-on-write clone support receive independent physical copies, trading extra disk space for the same isolation and correctness.
next_steps: Merge the integration lane and let each required platform seed its own native cache on the first cold validation.
Add cache status and pruning commands if normal development produces enough historical identities to make growth material.
